questions.title: Why is the model called "1.58-bit" instead of 2-bit?
questions.question_body: I am reading the paper "The Era of 1-bit LLMs" and I'm confused about the naming. The authors state that the weights are ternary, taking values from $\{-1, 0, 1\}$. In standard computing, representing three distinct values would require 2 bits. Why do they specifically call it "1.58-bit"?

questions.title: How does the "absmean" quantization function prevent weight collapse?
questions.question_body: I'm looking at the quantization formulas where $\widetilde{W} = \mathrm{RoundClip}(\frac{W}{\gamma + \epsilon}, -1, 1)$ and $\gamma = \frac{1}{nm}\sum_{ij} |W_{ij}|$. I understand that this scales the weights by their average absolute value before rounding. However, I'm struggling to see how this mechanism ensures a diverse distribution of $\{-1, 0, 1\}$ values across the weight matrix. If the weights are updated during training, doesn't this scaling factor $\gamma$ create a dependency between all weights in the matrix?

questions.title: Does BitNet b1.58 use quantization during training or only for inference?
questions.question_body: The paper mentions that BitNet b1.58 is "trained from scratch, with 1.58-bit weights." I am used to post-training quantization (PTQ) where a full-precision model is quantized after training. I am confused about how training works here. Are the weights strictly $\{-1, 0, 1\}$ during the backward pass, or are there "latent" full-precision weights that are quantized only during the forward pass to allow for gradient updates?

questions.title: How is matrix multiplication performed using only integer addition?
questions.question_body: The authors claim that the computation paradigm of BitNet b1.58 requires "almost no multiplication operations" and only involves integer addition. I understand that if a weight is $1$ or $-1$, multiplication is just addition or subtraction of the activation. But since the activations are 8-bit, how is this actually implemented in a way that provides a speedup over highly optimized FP16 GEMM kernels on a GPU?

questions.title: Clarification on the scaling law equivalence between 1.58-bit and FP16 models
questions.question_body: In the results section, the authors provide equivalences such as "13B BitNet b1.58 is more efficient... than 3B FP16 LLM." I am trying to understand the trade-off here. Even if the compute (FLOPs) is replaced by cheaper additions, a 13B model still has significantly more parameters to move from DRAM to SRAM than a 3B model. Does the reduced bit-width of the weights actually offset the increase in the total number of parameters when comparing latency and memory bandwidth?

questions.title: What is "zero-point quantization" in the context of activations?
questions.question_body: In the Quantization Function section, the authors mention that they scale activations to $[-Q_b, Q_b]$ per token to "get rid of the zero-point quantization." I am not familiar with zero-point quantization in this context. What exactly is a zero-point in activation quantization, and why does removing it make the implementation "more convenient and simple for system-level optimization"?
